text:
maria_cs: Customer ACME on Dedicated cluster `dc-ny` reporting intermittent 500s and high tail latency since ~2025-03-22T11:28:00Z. Example request IDs they saw: `r-0a1b2c3d`, `r-4e5f6g7h`. Can we gather repro steps + cluster logs?

alex_sre: on it. do we have a curl reproduction or a sample request payload? also which model and route?

maria_cs: route `/v1/generate` using model `rw-instruct-4k`, customer provided this curl (token redacted):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer ****REDACTED****' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"model":"rw-instruct-4k","input":"Summarize the quarterly results...","max_tokens":256,"temperature":0.0}'
```
They say it times out or returns 502/500 intermittently, usually at ~10-20s.

jamal_support: pinging customer for a narrow repro window and permission to collect debug bundle from their Dedicated cluster. asked for the exact timestamps (they sent logs): 2025-03-22T11:27:45Z -> 11:33:02Z.

alex_sre: OK. to start collecting from the cluster, run these (from control-plane with permissions):
```bash
# list inference pods and ages
kubectl -n redwood get pods -l app=redwood-inference -o wide

# grab recent logs for the pod that served the request (replace POD)
kubectl -n redwood logs POD_NAME --since=15m > /tmp/pod-POD_NAME.log

# describe pod to see restarts / events
kubectl -n redwood describe pod POD_NAME > /tmp/pod-POD_NAME.describe

# node-level dmesg and journal
ssh node-01 "sudo dmesg -T | tail -n 200" > /tmp/node-01-dmesg.log
ssh node-01 "sudo journalctl -u kubelet --since '30 minutes ago'" > /tmp/node-01-kubelet.log
```

ingrid_eng: add GPU diagnostics if pod is on GPU node:
```bash
# on the node
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,utilization.gpu,memory.used,memory.total --format=csv -l 1 -f /tmp/gpu-snapshot.csv & sleep 5; pkill -f nvidia-smi
# or a quick snapshot
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,utilization.gpu,memory.used,memory.total --format=csv
```

maria_cs: customer okayed debug bundle and gave exact request IDs again `r-0a1b2c3d` and `r-4e5f6g7h`. They also attached a short client-side trace with timestamps.

alex_sre: thanks. steps I'm running now: identify which pod handled `r-0a1b2c3d` via request-id logs in the ingress and route-proxy (examples):
```bash
# on ingress
kubectl -n ingress logs ingress-proxy-xyz --since=1h | grep r-0a1b2c3d
# on model router
kubectl -n redwood logs router-abc --since=1h | grep r-0a1b2c3d
```
If we find pod X, capture both container logs and the redis/kv cache logs on the pod. look for KV cache miss or backend errors.

sre-bot: [action] Created debug bundle: /var/backups/debug-bundles/debug-1748001234.tar.gz (encrypted).

jamal_support: pulling that bundle now. preparing to upload to support bucket. customer asked for ETA on fix; telling them we'll update after root cause.

alex_sre: pasted snippets found in pod logs around the request: (sanitized)
```
2025-03-22T11:28:01Z INFO request=r-0a1b2c3d router forwarding to pod redwood-inference-5f6d7c9
2025-03-22T11:28:05Z WARN request=r-0a1b2c3d kvcache miss for prefix=\"Summarize the quarterly\"
2025-03-22T11:28:12Z ERROR request=r-0a1b2c3d model-serving conversation crashed: OOMKilled (oom_reaped)
2025-03-22T11:28:13Z INFO container restart count=1
```

ingrid_eng: that OOMKilled lines up with GPU memory pressure seen on node-14: nvidia-smi snapshot during window:
```
index, name, utilization.gpu [%], memory.used [MiB], memory.total [MiB]
0, NVIDIA-A100, 98 %, 40634 MiB, 40960 MiB
```
Which explains the crash at ~11:28:12Z. also saw a pattern of large batch sizes from the router logs that spike memory.

maria_cs: forwarding this to customer. asked if they changed usage pattern — they said no, traffic steady but a spike of single big prompt batch hits at 11:27.

jamal_support: created a ticket to Dedicated infra to increase eviction buffer / tune oom_score_adj and asked for conservative autoscaling/queue backpressure for that customer. Ticket: DEDIC-2025-487.

alex_sre: immediate mitigation recommendations we gave customer:
- reduce batch size or add a hard token limit per request in their client
- pin to a lighter model variant (rw-instruct-2k) temporarily
- we enabled a temporary limit on concurrent requests per-account on their Dedicated cluster to avoid repeated OOMs

ingrid_eng: long-term: tune router batching heuristics, add dynamic memory headroom detection on GPU nodes, and surface per-customer batch histograms in Console.

maria_cs: customer accepted mitigation for now, wants final RCA and logs. I'll attach the debug bundle and the sanitized pod logs we captured.

jamal_support: uploaded sanitized bundle to S3: s3://redwood-support/dedicated-debug/1748001234-acme-debug.tar.gz (access granted to ACME support contact).

alex_sre: marking this resolved for now; will follow up once DEDIC-2025-487 has a fix plan. leaving notes for oncall: watch for repeated OOMKilled events on node-14 and similar pod names.

maria_cs: thanks everyone :heart: — I'll close the loop with the customer and paste the RCA when ready.

ingrid_eng: quick command summary (for docs):
```bash
kubectl -n redwood get pods -l app=redwood-inference -o wide
kubectl -n redwood logs <pod> --since=30m > pod.log
kubectl -n redwood describe pod <pod> > pod.describe
ssh <node> sudo dmesg -T | tail -n 200 > node.dmesg
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,utilization.gpu,memory.used,memory.total --format=csv
# bundle collector (example)
/usr/local/bin/redwood-debug-collector --namespace redwood --since 30m --output /tmp/debug-1748001234.tar.gz
```
